title: Staff Photonics Design Engineer at Lightmatter Sees Strategic Merit in Marvell’s Lumentum Acquisition but Flags Integration and AI Demand Risks
expert: Staff photonic IC engineer at Lightmatter (current; designs CPO/NPO optical engines)
verdict: A Lightmatter CPO designer (opinion-led, no Marvell purchases) backs the Lumentum deal as a hedge: DSPs are ~25%–30% of an 800G transceiver's cost and lose relevance as CPO/NPO/LPO adopt from end-2027, while Lumentum's InP fab is booked through early 2029 (hearsay).

Interconnect growth rate: DSP 25%–30% of 800G transceiver cost; CPO/NPO/LPO from end of 2027 (estimate), first read on DSP content at risk. → Tenet 2 (1.6T duopoly) ↓
Greenfield legs: Lumentum InP fab booked through early 2029 (hearsay), first read; owning it secures lasers for optical engines. → Tenet 3 (scale-up optics) ↑
Margins: integration one or two years (estimate) vs management's first-year non-GAAP EPS accretion (SB #65700): conflicting. → Tenet 4 (EPS compounding) ↓

changes: First read on Lumentum laser capacity sell-out (booked through early 2029, hearsay); no earlier expert call or stored row.
First read on DSP cost share (25%–30% of an 800G transceiver, estimate); no earlier expert call or stored row.
Integration one or two years and close in 2028 (estimate) vs management targeting non-GAAP EPS accretion in the first year after close (SB #65700): conflicting.
thesis_impact: Tenet 2 (interconnect >70%, 1.6T duopoly): ↓ — CPO/NPO/LPO from end-2027 reduces DSP need (25%–30% of 800G cost); customers may shift some DSP volume to Broadcom/Credo.
Tenet 3 (scale-up optics greenfield): ↑ — Lumentum lasers and optical engines capture the value moving away from DSPs.
Tenet 5 (bear flank): ↑ — customers avoid a single supplier; Coherent and Mitsubishi named for lasers, Chinese regulator approval a risk.
